He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State Shockers]]. Going undrafted in the [[2016 NBA draft]], he spent 3 seasons in the [[NBA]], playing for the [[New York Knicks]] and [[Washington Wizards]]. ==Early life== Born in [[Hays, Kansas]], Baker spent his early childhood in the small farming town of [[Utica, Kansas]], growing up with one sister and one brother. In a 2014 interview, he recalled, "I have memories of when was I very, very little, holding a basketball in my dog's doghouse when I was about 1." His father noted that he eventually gravitated toward basketball for practical reasons: "It was easier to haul him around and easier to get five or six to play basketball than to play baseball, where you'd need 12 to 14."{{cite news|first=Vahe|last=Gregorian|url=http://www.kansascity.com/2014/03/22/4909441/ron-baker-embodies-spirit-of-wichita.html|title=Ron Baker embodies spirit of Wichita State's second March in the national spotlight|newspaper=[[The Kansas City Star]]|date=March 22, 2014|access-date=March 23, 2014|url-status=bot: unknown|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140326084428/http://www.kansascity.com/2014/03/22/4909441/ron-baker-embodies-spirit-of-wichita.html|archive-date=March 26, 2014}} ==High school career== While he developed into a star at [[Scott Community High]], and dreamed of playing for the state's premier college program at [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], he was slow to grow into his body; by the end of his junior year, he was only {{convert|6|ft|m}} tall, and had drawn interest from only two [[NCAA Division I|Division I]] programs: [[Little Rock Trojans men's basketball|Arkansas–Little Rock]] and [[South Dakota State Jackrabbits men's basketball|South Dakota State]]. However, he grew to {{convert|6|ft|3|in|m|abbr=on}} during the summer between his junior and senior seasons. In his senior year, Baker helped the team finish with a 25–1 record. In return, he was named 3A First-Team All-State in [[Kansas]]. The peak of his high school basketball career was when he hit a game winning put-back buzzer beater against [[Minneapolis High School]] to win the Class 3A state basketball championship, finishing the game with 26 points and 9 rebounds. As a result, Baker helped the school win its first ever Class 3A Championship, although the school had made two different appearances in the past.{{cite web|first=Rod|last=Haxton|url=http://www.scottcountyrecord.com/sports/baker-hits-game-winner-for-3a-state-title|title=Baker hits game winner for 3A state title|work=ScottyCountyRecord.com|date=March 13, 2011|access-date=August 27, 2014}} Nonetheless, Baker remained little-known among Division I coaches. ''[[ESPN.com]]'' writer Eamonn Brennan noted in 2014,{{cite web|first=Eamonn|last=Brennan|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/11388367/talent-evaluation-come-long-way-remains-inexact-science|title=The art of talent evaluation|work=ESPN.com|date=August 27, 2014|access-date=August 27, 2014}}
ESPN's RecruitingNation maintains detailed scouting reports on hundreds of the best high school basketball players in the country. . . . Ron Baker's profile read as follows:

"Will walk-on at Wichita State in 2011–12 and spend a redshirt year. Expected to be on scholarship starting in 2012–13."

And that was it. Next to Baker's name was "NR," which stands for "Not Ranked." The same abbreviation sits next to secondary lists for "position," "regional" and "state." Baker — who requested a redshirt year when he committed, as a walk-on, to Wichita State in April 2011 — couldn't have been more off the recruiting radar.
After his senior season, Kansas invited him to visit the campus. Baker had thoughts about [[Walk-on (sports)|walking on]] there, but the invitation occurred during the middle of his high school baseball season. Baker's father recalled that Ron felt that his basketball game was rusty, and that "he didn't want to embarrass himself" in a potential scrimmage. ==College career== {{multiple image | image1=Ron Baker (basketball) 2013.jpg | width1 = 160 | image2=20150111 Ron Baker (6) cropped.jpg | width2 = 223 | footer = Baker as a [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] freshman for the [[2012–13 Wichita State Shockers men's basketball team|2012–13 Wichita State Shockers]] (left) and 4th-year junior for the [[2014–15 Wichita State Shockers men's basketball team|2014–15 team]] (right) }} Baker chose to play for the [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State Shockers]] after also having interest in Arkansas–Little Rock, [[Eastern Illinois Panthers men's basketball|Eastern Illinois]], and South Dakota State.{{cite web|url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/maple/125003|title=Ron Baker – Rivals.com|work=Rivals.com|access-date=December 18, 2015}} Rather than playing in his first season with the Shockers, Baker redshirted after a reluctant approval from head coach [[Gregg Marshall]]. In his first season, Baker emerged as one of the elite free-throw shooters at Wichita State. He finished the season shooting for a free-throw percentage of .822, the highest for a qualified player on the team. Baker did not prove himself to be an efficient scorer and played just eighteen games in the entire season due to a [[stress fracture]] in his left foot.{{cite web|url=http://www.goshockers.com/news/2012/12/18/205835905.aspx|title=MBB: Ron Baker Diagnosed with Stress Fracture|work=GoShockers.com|date=December 18, 2012|access-date=December 18, 2012}} He eventually played a major role when the Shockers made an unanticipated run into the semifinals of the [[2013 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]]. Baker shot 40 percent from the field, 42.9 percent on three-pointers, most notably scoring 16 points in a huge win over No. 1 [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] (tied for team-high). He earned no major awards by the time the season came to a close. Entering the [[2013–14 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]], Baker became known as one of the [[Missouri Valley Conference|MVC]]'s premier shooters. He, [[Cleanthony Early]], and [[Fred VanVleet]] led the team in scoring and had a major influence on [[2013–14 Wichita State Shockers men's basketball team|Wichita State]]'s season, which saw the Shockers become the first NCAA Division I men's team to enter the NCAA tournament undefeated in [[1990–91 UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball team|over 20 years]]. Baker was named to the 2014 [[Missouri Valley Conference|MVC]] All-Conference First Team and the [[CBE Hall of Fame Classic]]'s Most Valuable Player after finishing his first season with a double-digit scoring average. After the Shockers' season ended in the NCAA tournament at the hands of [[2013–14 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]] and its highly touted freshman class, Baker indicated that one of the Wildcats' top recruits, [[Aaron Harrison]], told him, "You are a bad, bad, bad boy." He was a part of three Missouri Valley Conference championships (2013, 2014, 2015), nine NCAA Tournament wins, two trips to the Sweet 16 (2013, 2015) and a trip to the 2013 Final Four. As a senior in 2015–16, he averaged 14.0 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.2 assists, and 1.51 steals over 31.6 minutes in 35 games. His postseason honors included: John R. Wooden Second Team All-American; USA Today Second Team All-American and 2015 finalist for Jerry West Award. Baker also represented the United States at the 2015 Pan American Games, where he started all five games and won a bronze medal.{{cite web|first=Paul|last=Suellentrop|url=http://www.kansas.com/sports/college/wichita-state/article28777519.html|title=Wichita State's Ron Baker makes big impression at Pan Am Games|work=Kansas.com|date=July 26, 2016|access-date=July 26, 2016}} ==Professional career== ===New York Knicks (2016–2018)=== [[File:John Wall, Ron Baker (32518326061).jpg|thumb|Baker guards [[John Wall]] of the [[Washington Wizards]] in 2017]] After going undrafted in the [[2016 NBA draft]], Baker joined the [[New York Knicks]] for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/knicks/knicks-participate-orlando-pro-summer-league|title=Knicks to Participate in Orlando Pro Summer League|work=NBA.com|date=June 27, 2016|access-date=June 27, 2016}} Despite a scattered Summer League campaign,{{cite web|first=Marc|last=Berman|url=https://nypost.com/2016/10/21/ron-baker-makes-knicks-roster-over-chasson-randle/|title=Ron Baker makes Knicks roster over Chasson Randle|work=NYPost.com|date=October 21, 2016|access-date=October 26, 2016}} Baker signed with the Knicks on August 1, 2016,{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/knicks/knicks-sign-ron-baker|title=Knicks Sign Ron Baker|work=NBA.com|date=August 1, 2016|access-date=August 1, 2016}} and secured an opening-night roster spot. He made his debut for the Knicks in their season opener on October 25, 2016, recording five points and one rebound in seven minutes off the bench in a 117–88 loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400899375|title=Knicks vs. Cavaliers – Box Score|work=ESPN.com|date=October 25, 2016|access-date=October 25, 2016}} On December 15, 2016, he scored a career-high 13 points in a 103–90 loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/bakerro01/gamelog/2017/|title=Ron Baker 2016-17 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=January 16, 2017}} On January 16, 2017, he made his first career start for the Knicks and subsequently scored 12 points in a 108–107 loss to the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. During his rookie and sophomore seasons, in which he became a fan favorite, he was assigned multiple times to New York's [[NBA G League|D-League/G League]] affiliate, the [[Westchester Knicks]].{{cite web|url=http://gleague.nba.com/all-time-nba-assignments/|title=All-Time NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=January 2, 2018}}{{cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/nba/teams/New-York-Knicks/20/Transaction_History/2018|title=2017-2018 New York Knicks Transactions History|work=RealGM.com|access-date=April 15, 2018}} On August 7, 2017, Baker re-signed with the Knicks.{{cite web|title=Knicks Re-Sign Ron Baker|url=http://www.nba.com/knicks/knick-re-sign-ron-baker|website=NBA.com|date=August 7, 2017|access-date=August 7, 2017}} Baker missed the Knicks' game on January 2, 2018, against the [[San Antonio Spurs]] because of a broken left orbital bone sustained when he was hit in the face trying to stop [[Anthony Davis]]' drive to the basket in New York's victory against the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] on December 30.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975296|title=Spurs beat Knicks, Popovich alone in 5th for coaching wins|work=ESPN.com|date=January 2, 2018|access-date=January 2, 2018}} On February 5, 2018, he was ruled out for the rest of the season after it was determined he required right shoulder surgery.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2018/02/05/knicks-ron-baker-right-shoulder-surgery-out-season/#/|title=New York Knicks' Ron Baker to have shoulder surgery, miss rest of season|work=NBA.com|date=February 5, 2018|access-date=February 5, 2018}} Baker was waived by the Knicks on December 13, 2018.{{cite web |title=Knicks sign rookie Trier to guaranteed NBA deal, waive Baker |url=https://apnews.com/cac373ab1dca4d8490011546d093427c |website=AP News |access-date=December 14, 2018 |date=December 13, 2018}} ===Washington Wizards (2018–2019)=== On December 20, 2018, Baker signed with the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-sign-ron-baker|title=Wizards sign Ron Baker|work=NBA.com|date=December 20, 2018|access-date=December 21, 2018}} He was waived on January 7, 2019, after appearing in four games. ===CSKA Moscow (2019–2020)=== On August 1, 2019, he signed a contract with [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]] of the [[VTB United League]] and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/cska-moscow-signs-ron-baker/|title=Cska Moscow signs Ron Baker|date=August 1, 2019|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=August 9, 2019}} Baker averaged 2.5 points per game in 27 EuroLeague games. On May 27, 2020, he parted ways with the team.{{cite web |title=CSKA Moscow, Ron Baker part ways |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/cska-moscow-ron-baker-part-ways/ |website=Sportando |access-date=May 27, 2020 |date=May 27, 2020}} ==National team career== Baker represented the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States national team]] at the [[Basketball at the 2015 Pan American Games – Men's tournament|2015 Pan American Games]], where he won a bronze medal. == Retirement == In a May 2021 episode of ''Inside TBT'', the official podcast of [[The Basketball Tournament]], Baker indicated that he had retired from play. He told the hosts that he had undergone hip surgery while overseas, and wanted to move on with his life, with hopes of entering the business world. He is serving as general manager of AfterShocks, a TBT team made up mostly of Wichita State basketball alumni, in the [[The Basketball Tournament 2021|2021 TBT]]. Baker also emphasized that he would not play in this or any future edition of TBT.{{cite podcast |url=https://thetournament.com/news/inside-tbt-episode-19-ron-baker-discusses-joining-the-aftershocks-for-tbt-2021/ |title=Inside TBT Episode 19: Ron Baker Discusses Joining the AfterShocks for TBT 2021 |website= |publisher=The Basketball Tournament |host= |date=May 19, 2021 |time= |access-date=June 24, 2021}} In August 2021, Baker was named project manager in the strategy and business development department at a medical center, Ascension Via Christi, in [[Wichita, Kansas]].{{Cite web |last=Askounis |first=Johnny |date=2021-08-25 |title=Ron Baker retires at 28, steps into healthcare |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1240735/former-cska-player-ron-baker-retires-at-28/ |access-date=2025-01-02 |website=Eurohoops}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} .801 || 4.2 || 2.8 || 1.3 || .6 || 13.2 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Baker is an enrolled member of the [[Citizen Potawatomi Nation]].{{cite web|url=https://indiancountrymedianetwork.com/culture/sports/ron-baker-native-americas-next-nba-star//|title=Ron Baker Is Native America's Next NBA Star|work=indiancountrymedianetwork.com|access-date=September 24, 2017}} Following the 2015–16 season, Baker was contacted by the owner of a small publishing house in [[El Dorado, Kansas]], who wanted him to write a children's book. The final product, ''You're Too Big to Dream Small'', is an illustrated book with rhyming text written primarily by Baker himself and based closely on his life. It was released on August 3, 2016, and Baker personally signed the first print run of 6,000 copies.{{cite news|first=Denise|last=Neil|url=http://www.kansas.com/entertainment/article88427772.html|title=Ron Baker: NBA recruit and children's book author|newspaper=[[The Wichita Eagle]]|date=July 8, 2016|access-date=October 25, 2016}} Ron Baker married Liv Nielsen in 2023.
